evidence: app/src/pages/ability.ts:1-16 — the ability page itself is one self-contained file, easy to delete
app/src/main.ts:8 — the only import of it; app/src/main.ts:29 the only route entry
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:132-145 — abilitiesSection with /abilities links lives inside the Pokémon page, must be edited too
app/src/server.mjs:21 — ROUTES regex whitelist duplicates the client route table; must be updated or the server 404s the shell
app/src/components.ts:27-29 — CardData.hidden / 'Hidden ability' note is consumed only by the ability page; dead code if the feature is dropped
removability.rationale: Removing a feature means deleting one file plus a handful of small, findable edits across 5-6 files, and several pieces (hidden flag, Ability interface, .card__note CSS) silently go dead rather than being removed with the feature.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:21-31 — pokemonCardLink is the single place every card sprite is chosen (via api.ts:11 spriteUrl)
app/src/components.ts:51-65 — cardsFromPokemon resolves pokemon refs to species cards once, reused by move/ability/type pages
app/src/server.mjs:21 vs app/src/main.ts:21-29 — route list maintained in two places; a new client route silently gets a 404 status from the server
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:20 and app/src/pages/team.ts:16 — default-variety lookup ('varieties.find(is_default)') duplicated verbatim
app/src/pages/team.ts:87-110 — team page re-implements the card list markup instead of going through cardList (components.ts:37)
changeability.rationale: The likely bug classes (sprite choice, name humanization, caching, formatting) each land in one obvious module; the residual duplication (routes, variety lookup, team card list) means a few small things get fixed twice.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:123-133 — pages depend only on get/getByName plus typed interfaces; caching is fully encapsulated
app/src/team.ts:7-56 — team state is one explicit module with pure get/add/remove functions; pages don't touch localStorage directly
app/src/main.ts:12-17 — PageContext (main, url, isCurrent) is a narrow, documented seam between router and pages
app/src/server.mjs:1-30 — server is plain Node, fully separated from the TS client; but ROUTES at :21 hard-codes the client router's paths
app/src/pages/home.ts:1-4 — pages import only api/components/dom/format/main types; no page imports another page
coupling.rationale: Loosely coupled, narrow interfaces and explicit shared state; the one real tangle is the server's duplicate knowledge of the client's route list.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:51-65 — cardsFromPokemon(items, ref, extra?) models the actual variation (ability hidden flag, type/move ref shapes) via callbacks instead of flags
app/src/components.ts:39-42 — countLine(n, noun) and section(title, children, attrs) are small composable abstractions used by every page
app/src/format.ts:1-55 — pure, testable formatters (humanize, englishName, latestEnglishFlavorText, orDash) shared everywhere
app/src/pages/team.ts:87-110 — the one place an abstraction failed to stretch: cardList can't take per-item extras, so the markup is copied
app/src/dom.ts:6-30 — h() is a minimal, adequate DOM seam with on* handling and child flattening
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions are designed around the app's real variation and stretch to a Moves-shaped Items section with mostly reuse; only cardList's lack of a per-item hook caused copy-paste.

findings.issue: The server's ROUTES regex list duplicates the client route table in app/src/main.ts:21-29; adding a route requires two synchronized edits, and forgetting one yields a valid page served with HTTP 404.
findings.suggestion: Export the route patterns from a single module imported by both, or derive the server list from the client table; at minimum add a comment in both files pointing at each other.

findings.issue: The team page hand-rolls the same ul.card-grid/li.card-item markup that cardList (components.ts:37) produces, duplicating card markup that must stay visually in sync.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardList with an optional per-item content callback (or accept a wrapper around each card) so the team page reuses it.

findings.issue: Default-variety resolution ('species.varieties.find(is_default) ?? varieties[0]' plus the pokemon fetch) is duplicated from app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:20-23.
findings.suggestion: Add a defaultPokemon(species) helper in api.ts and call it from both pages.

findings.issue: CardData.hidden and the 'Hidden ability' note exist solely to serve the ability page; if Abilities are ever removed this becomes dead code that survives the deletion.
findings.suggestion: Accept the flag via the extra callback only where needed, or note in CardData that it's ability-page-specific.

findings.issue: The API base default 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in app/src/server.mjs:12 (the injector) and api.ts:8 (the fallback), so changing the default means two edits.
findings.suggestion: Keep the literal only in server.mjs and let the client fail loudly when the meta tag is missing in production.

findings.issue: EAGER_CARDS = 120 is a magic number implicitly tied to PAGE_SIZE 48 (home.ts:7) with no cross-reference.
findings.suggestion: Define it as e.g. 2.5 pages of PAGE_SIZE, or comment the relationship.

findings.issue: main.ts both defines the router and the PageContext/navigate/renderNotFound types and values that every page imports, creating a mild hub (type-only at runtime, but a real dependency cycle in the module graph).
findings.suggestion: Move PageContext/PageResult and shared render helpers into their own module (e.g. routing.ts) imported by main and pages alike.

summary: A genuinely editable no-framework app: one data layer with an encapsulated cache, pure formatters, and a shared card/section abstraction that every page composes, so the highest-value fixes (sprites, names, caching, formatting) land in exactly one file. The main costs are small duplications — a client/server route list kept in sync by hand, a copied default-variety lookup, and a team page that bypasses cardList. Removing a feature is the weakest scenario, requiring edits in five or six files and leaving some near-dead code behind.
